subject.title: `claude-cli` backend: `ownsNativeCompaction` assumption is false for `claude -p` sessions — nobody compacts, sessions grow past 200% context, and every recovery path (stuck-session abort, safeguard compaction) fails silently

question: When a Claude print-mode session remains over its measured context budget, should OpenClaw fall back to its context engine or continue deferring exclusively to Claude Code?
rationale: The exclusive-deferral contract is disproven by field evidence, but unconditional OpenClaw compaction can conflict with Claude's native resumable state; maintainers must choose the permanent ownership and fallback behavior.

options.title: Measured native fallback
options.body: Prefer Claude native compaction, but fall back to OpenClaw compaction or rotate the binding when token accounting shows no reduction after the threshold is crossed.

options.title: OpenClaw owns compaction
options.body: Remove Claude CLI native ownership and always compact the OpenClaw transcript before subsequent CLI turns.

options.title: Claude remains exclusive owner
options.body: Keep unconditional deferral and limit changes to diagnostics, user notification, and stricter supported-Claude requirements.

recommendation.title: Measured native fallback
recommendation.body: Prefer Claude native compaction, but fall back to OpenClaw compaction or rotate the binding when token accounting shows no reduction after the threshold is crossed.

likelyOwner.reason: This person landed the current ownership contract and is the strongest available owner for deciding whether it should become conditional or be replaced.
